routes.label: Count complete weeks and extra days

question: Suppose July of year \(N\) has five Mondays. Which of the following must occur five times in August of year \(N?\) (Note: both months have \(31\) days.)
solution:
Since \(31=4\cdot7+3\), a 31-day month contains four complete weeks and three extra days. Consequently, the weekdays of its first three dates occur five times, and every other weekday occurs four times.

For Monday to occur five times in July, July must begin on Saturday, Sunday, or Monday. Moving forward 31 days advances the weekday by three places, because 28 days make four complete weeks. Thus all possibilities are:

July starts Saturday: August starts Tuesday, and Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday occur five times in August.

July starts Sunday: August starts Wednesday, and Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday occur five times in August.

July starts Monday: August starts Thursday, and Thursday, Friday, and Saturday occur five times in August.

Thursday appears in all three lists, and no other weekday does. Therefore \(\boxed{\text{Thursday}}\) must occur five times, choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
